title: Chemical Changes: Word Equations and Reaction Understanding
topic: Chemical Changes - Word Equations and Basic Reactions
subject: Science

questions.question: In the word equation: magnesium + oxygen → magnesium oxide, which substances are the reactants?
questions.explanation: Reactants are the starting substances written on the left side of the arrow. Magnesium and oxygen react together to form magnesium oxide.

questions.question: In the word equation: magnesium + oxygen → magnesium oxide, which substance is the product?
questions.explanation: Products are the new substances formed, written on the right side of the arrow. Magnesium oxide is the only product in this reaction.

questions.question: A student heats copper carbonate strongly. The green powder turns black and a gas is produced that forms white solids in limewater. Which word equation represents this reaction?
options: copper carbonate + oxygen → copper oxide + carbon dioxide
copper carbonate → copper oxide + carbon dioxide
copper oxide + carbon dioxide → copper carbonate
questions.explanation: This is thermal decomposition. One reactant (copper carbonate) breaks down into two products when heated. Heat is a condition, not a reactant, so it is not written on the left side.

questions.question: A student adds dilute hydrochloric acid to zinc metal. Bubbles of gas are observed. Which word equation correctly represents this reaction?
options: hydrochloric acid + zinc → zinc chloride + hydrogen
hydrochloric acid + zinc → zinc chloride + water
hydrochloric acid + zinc → zinc hydride + chlorine
questions.explanation: When acid reacts with a metal, the products are a salt and hydrogen gas. The salt name combines the metal name with the acid name (hydrochloric acid produces chloride salts).

questions.question: A student adds dilute sulfuric acid to calcium carbonate. Bubbles of gas are produced. Which gas is produced?
questions.explanation: When acid reacts with a carbonate, carbon dioxide gas is produced. This can be confirmed by bubbling the gas through limewater which turns milky.

questions.question: Which word equation correctly represents the reaction between nitric acid and sodium hydroxide?
options: nitric acid + sodium hydroxide → sodium nitrate + water
nitric acid + sodium hydroxide → sodium nitrate + hydrogen
nitric acid + sodium hydroxide → sodium nitrate + carbon dioxide
nitric acid + sodium → sodium nitrate + water
questions.explanation: This is neutralisation (acid + alkali). The products are always a salt and water. The salt name combines the metal from the alkali with the acid name (nitric acid produces nitrate salts).

questions.question: A student observes that iron nails rust faster when placed in salt water compared to fresh water. What does this observation suggest?
options: Salt water has no effect on rusting
Salt water speeds up the rusting process
questions.explanation: The observation shows that rusting occurs faster in salt water. Dissolved salts act as a catalyst that speeds up the oxidation reaction between iron, oxygen and water.

questions.question: In the reaction: glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water + thermal energy, which elements are present in the reactants?
questions.explanation: Glucose contains carbon, hydrogen and oxygen. Oxygen gas contains oxygen. These are the only elements in the reactants, and the same elements must be present in the products.

questions.question: Why can nitrogen gas NOT be produced when magnesium burns in air?
options: Nitrogen is too heavy to be produced
Nitrogen is not present in the reactants
Nitrogen is a liquid at room temperature
Nitrogen reacts too quickly with magnesium
questions.explanation: In chemical reactions, atoms are rearranged but not created or destroyed. Only elements present in the reactants can appear in the products. Magnesium and oxygen do not contain nitrogen.

questions.question: A student heats potassium chlorate (KClO3) strongly. Oxygen gas is produced. Which type of reaction is this?
questions.explanation: Thermal decomposition is when a single substance breaks down into simpler substances when heated. One reactant produces two or more products.

questions.question: Which observation provides evidence that a chemical reaction has occurred when acid is added to carbonate?
options: The volume of liquid mixture increases
questions.explanation: Production of a new gas (seen as bubbles) indicates a new substance has been formed, which is evidence of a chemical change. Temperature change alone could be physical.

questions.question: In the word equation for photosynthesis: carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen, what condition is required?
questions.explanation: Light energy is required for photosynthesis. It is written above the arrow as a condition, not on the left side as a reactant, because light is not consumed in the reaction.

questions.question: A student tests a gas with a lit splint. The flame is extinguished with a pop sound. Which reaction most likely produced this gas?
questions.explanation: The pop test confirms hydrogen gas. Hydrogen is produced when acid reacts with a metal. Acid + carbonate produces carbon dioxide (limewater test), acid + alkali produces no gas.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes what happens to atoms during a chemical reaction?
options: Atoms are created during the reaction
Atoms are destroyed during the reaction
Atoms are rearranged but not created or destroyed
Atoms change into different types of atoms
questions.explanation: Chemical reactions involve rearrangement of atoms. The same types and number of atoms are present in reactants and products. This is why mass is conserved.

questions.question: A student writes this word equation: copper + oxygen → copper oxide. What information is missing?
options: The condition (heat) needed for the reaction
The state symbols for each substance
questions.explanation: Copper does not react with oxygen at room temperature. Heat is required to start the reaction. Conditions are written above the arrow in word equations.

questions.question: Which word equation correctly represents neutralisation?
options: acid + carbonate → salt + water + carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: Neutralisation is specifically the reaction between an acid and an alkali. The products are always a salt and water. No gas is produced in neutralisation.

questions.question: A student observes a colour change from green to black when heating a powder. The gas produced forms white precipitate in limewater milky. What was the original powder?
questions.explanation: Copper carbonate is green. When heated, it decomposes to black copper oxide and carbon dioxide gas. Carbon dioxide turns limewater milky. This matches all observations.

questions.question: In the reaction: hydrochloric acid + sodium hydroxide → sodium chloride + water, which elements are present in the products?
questions.explanation: Sodium chloride contains sodium and chlorine. Water contains hydrogen and oxygen. These same elements must be present in the reactants (hydrochloric acid and sodium hydroxide).

questions.question: Which condition is needed for rusting but NOT for combustion?
questions.explanation: Rusting requires both oxygen AND water. Combustion requires oxygen and a fuel, plus heat to start, but water is not required. Rusting is a slow oxidation that occurs at room temperature.

questions.question: A student claims that heating calcium carbonate produces calcium, carbon and oxygen gas. Why is this claim incorrect?
options: The products should be calcium oxide and carbon dioxide, not separate elements
Calcium carbonate does not react when heated
Oxygen gas cannot be produced from heating
Carbon cannot be produced from a carbonate
questions.explanation: In thermal decomposition, compounds break into simpler compounds, not necessarily into elements. Calcium carbonate decomposes to calcium oxide (a compound) and carbon dioxide (a compound), not to separate elements.
